key_insight: EDIT-B combines RNA editing biomarkers with machine learning to distinguish bipolar disorder from major depressive disorder; this is psychiatric diagnostic research, not cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: The test could complement psychiatric assessment during depressive episodes, but effects on diagnostic delays and patient outcomes remain unproven in the supplied abstract.
method: Integrates clinical metadata with A-to-I RNA editing signatures in eight genes.
Evaluated against physician diagnoses in an independent, double-blind cohort across four European centers.
Uses explainability and sensitivity analyses to assess model drivers.
evidence_signal: Among 393 patients (155 bipolar disorder; 238 major depressive disorder), EDIT-B achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.873 (95% CI 0.837–0.909), 82.6% sensitivity and 80.3% specificity.
watch_item: Validation against physician diagnoses does not establish whether routine use improves diagnostic decisions or patient outcomes.
paper_title: EDIT-B Consortium: An External Pan-European Validation of an Innovative Machine Learning-Based Test for Bipolar Disorder Diagnosis
